Attention all 40k fans, now you finally have the chance to join the ranks of the Space Marines and impose the Emperor's will... personally. Covered in power armour, weilding formidable arsenal and swinging  deadly chainswords or power weapons Space Marine really delivers on all our fantasies of being a one-man army reaking havock over the battlefield as one of the Imperial's finest. 

Fortunately you are not as invincible as the codex leads Ultramarine fans to believe, but man... you are pretty darn close. In terms of gameplay there are a few challenges along the way requiring some planning and tactics, however in most situations you will find strategic thinning of high risk targets from a sniper or a las cannon followed by brute force carnage is the best way to go. Well atleast after you have replace the combat knife with a more fitting close combat weapon anyway. 

The combat overall whilst generally being repetitive was alot of fun, I can not express how much enjoyment I got out of bludgeoning swarms of enemies with my Thunder Hammer.  On higher difficulties some skill and to be honest a bit of luck comes into play during the larger battles or boss fights in later portions of the game. Prepare to have to redo some of these atleast a couple of times before you are able to anhiliate all the threats. The final boss fight in particular had me quite frustrated, but at 2am a lot of my deaths could have just been down to fatigue.

The storyline was above the generic hack and slash standard capitalising on the rich 40K universe. That coupled with some interesting twists and turns scattered throughout the game compeled me to ritually stay up late on week nights until I had finished the game. 

In summary I was very pleased the game and I was dissapointed I didn't pick it up earlier due to some negative reveiws I had heard from others. The game was deffinately underated and the ending left me wishing a sequel was released by THQ, but hopefully our Nordic friends with the rights to the beloved 40k universe will release one in the future.
Ever since I played the first Dawn of War, I've always LOVED the Thunder Hammer and I've always wanted to use it...NOW YOU CAN

Do you enjoy decapitating orcs? How about xenophobic giant freaking space marines? Incredibly satisfying gameplay? A multiplayer that is surprisingly addictive? Or maybe you just need an outlet for your testosterone fueled rage.

Whatever the case, this game is awesome, played by only the manliest of men and feared by sissies and milkdrinkers worldwide.

If you do not like feeling awesome or facing off against thousands of ugly greenskinned mutts, this game may not be for you. If you enjoy undisclosed action however, I would love to kick your butt in the multiplayer!

Follow the amazing tale of Colonel Buff Mclargehuge as he progresses down elevators, Up elevators, through doors, through other doors, And fights many Orkz. Be wary for Colonel Buff McLargehuges weakness are BOMBSQUIGS something that there will be about 50 of per area you enter. They will kill you in one or two explosions.
Unbelievably good! Every bit of this game is as satisfying as the next.

In this game you get to play an emotionally unavailable frat boy/space marine who ponderously wanders through the  industrial underbelly of the 40k universe murdering everything in sight. It is exactly as fun as it sounds, get it!

Good game for warhammer 40K fans out there.  Lots of blood and gore.  I find the campaign very disappointingly short though.  The multiplayer is buggy on some maps and it sucks that you can't choose the map that you want!  Wtf?  Needs a lot of improvement!
Usually when I play a so called 40k pc game, they sadly fail to portray the unique world and sheer awesomeness... I am happy to say that playing this erased the memory of those failures from my mind.

So, I have this to ask of you. Why haven't you gotten this? Have you at least tried out the demo? No? *Smacks you upside the head* Go try it! It's a gore filled, bloody as Hell (No, wait, it's Orks. But oh, how they bleed.), and it's a VERY simple control system that'll have you taking on Hordes of Orks in maybe a minute after the start.

And speaking from my experience on the 360 version, the Online is INCREDIBLY fun (Though I was limited due to buying the game used), and, believe it or not, I could find people. Yes. Actual people. In ALL the game modes I had. Exterminatus, Versus, the likes. Even though I was level 5 most of the time, I was doing a large amount of work for my team, keeping them well placed. I can only wonder what I would've been like at a higher level, with more weapons... <3

And then I get to the campaign. It's a camping trip gone astra- And I'm going to stop there. No, it's a typical Warhammer 40,000 story. Orks, suddenly, *Censored*. Whoah. Since I'm still new to the series, it caught me off guard, but, hey. It's still well done. The final fight is a gory mess of blood and fun and gore. But that final game movie, it's a painful one. The people in Warhammer 40,000, especially Space Marines, are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. No bars hold, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. GLORIFIED ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, them Space Marines are. But somehow, Relic has, once again, created a sort of relate-able glorified ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who has a heart of light (Or so we may think, depending on how you take the game.), and is a good character for the 40,000 universe. Upon arriving to the first Guardsmen outpost, he tells the lead Guardsman there that they saved themselves, and told him to rise. Captain Titus seems to treat Guardsmen as a form of little brother. It's very amusing to me.

And oh my Emperor, the music. The music is very much, to me, the highlight of Space Marine. It's an absolute blast to listen to, and every second of it sends chills down my spine. It's like listening to Dawn of War II's "The Green Horde Rises" in 19 songs, ESPECIALLY "A Hero's Legacy". Holy crap (That plays during the end video, before the credits).

Over all? I'd recommend getting it while on sale, but get it. It may not be your cup of tea, but try the Demo out. The two levels included (Well, level and a half because of the SHEER size of the Jump pack mission in game) are essentially copied and pasted out of the game itself. They give you a basic understanding of how the game works, and plenty of ways to test your skill.
